en: So to be very clear about the difference
between AI workflows and AI agents, both of
course may use AI. Agents certainly will. AI
is a central part of an AI agent. A workflow
could also work without AI depending on what
it does.
The difference is how much the LLM is
allowed to decide or what the role of the
LLM is in general. So in a workflow, the AI
model decides nothing. You do, you build the
workflow, you set up the steps.
In an AI agent, the model decides everything
in the end. You give it some task and then
the agent loop runs as you learned earlier
and decides how to tackle that task and how
to work through it. So the AI is the brain
in an AI agent. In a workflow, it may be
part of one step, but it may also not be.
And it certainly does not decide what
happens when.
Because the steps in a workflow, as
mentioned, are fixed. They are set by the
developer, by you if you're building the
workflow.
In an AI agent, on the other hand, you have
an agent with tools and that agent decides
what to do when and if something should
happen at all.
The tools are also important. A workflow is
absolutely not about tool because it's not
about an AI brain. It's not about an agent.
So there are no tools. There are just the
predefined steps. An AI agent, on the other
hand, is all about these tools as explained.
And the model's job in an AI workflow,
therefore, if at all,
is to perform one specific task. For
example, if you have a workflow that is
about summarizing text, then an LLM may be
used to summarize the text in one of the
workflow steps.
Nothing else. It's not the brain powering
the workflow. It's just a workhorse that may
be used in one or more steps. Again,
depending on what the workflow does.
In the agent, on the other hand, it is that
brain.
And if you run a workflow multiple times, if
it gets triggered multiple times,
the sequence will always be the same. It's
totally deterministic. Sure, if you have one
step in a workflow where AI is used, for
example, for summarizing text, you may get
different summaries for the same text
because LLMs are not deterministic, but the
sequence of steps in the workflow will
always be the same. In an AI agent, on the
other hand, the agent may choose a totally
different path for working through a
problem, even if you give it the same
problem multiple times.
So it's not deterministic. That's a core
difference.
